cover.title: The Way Back Home
cover.subtitle: A true story from the Bible

text: In the very beginning, God made everything.
He made the sky, the trees, the flowers, and the birds.
Then God made a man named Adam and a woman named Eve.
God loved them, and they loved being with Him.
Their garden home, Eden, was perfect.
God gave Adam and Eve every tree in the garden to enjoy.
Only one tree was not for them.
“Do not eat from that tree,” God said. “If you do, you will die.”
It was one simple rule from a Father who loved them.
One day, a sneaky serpent spoke to Eve.
“Did God really say that?” he asked.
“That fruit won’t hurt you. It will make you like God!”
But the serpent was lying.
He wanted Eve to stop trusting God.
Eve looked at the fruit. It looked so good.
She took a bite.
Then she gave some to Adam, and he ate it too.
Uh-oh. For the very first time, people had disobeyed God.
The Bible calls this sin.
Sin changed everything.
Adam and Eve felt ashamed and afraid.
That day God made clothes for them from animal skins.
Those animals died so Adam and Eve could be covered.
God already had a plan to bring His people home.
Adam and Eve had children, and their children had children, all the way down to you and me.
Every person is born with sin inside.
Sin is like marks we cannot rub off.
It makes us want our own way instead of God’s way.
People tried hard to get clean.
They tried being extra good.
They tried to scrub and wash and try again.
But no matter how hard they tried, the marks stayed.
Nobody can wash sin away all by themselves.
Sin is like a giant wall between people and God.
God is perfectly good, and sin cannot come close to Him.
The Bible says sin leads to death, which means being far away from God forever.
That is very sad news.
But it is not the end of the story!
Here is the good news!
God loved the world so much that He sent His only Son, Jesus.
Jesus is the door in the wall.
People who know Jesus tell everyone, “Come and see! There is a way back to God!”
Jesus never sinned, not even once.
But He chose to die on a cross.
He took the punishment for our sin, so we would not have to.
The cross is where the way home begins.
Every person has a choice to make.
Some people pray, “God, I am sorry for my sin. I believe Jesus died for me. Please save me!”
Other people say, “No thanks.”
Jesus loves everyone, and He lets each person choose.
Three days after Jesus died, His friends found His tomb empty.
Jesus was alive again! He beat sin and death.
Everyone who trusts Jesus is washed clean.
All the marks are gone!
He gives them a brand-new start.
One day, everyone who trusts Jesus will be with Him forever.
Heaven’s gates will be wide open.
And Jesus will be right there, holding out His hands to welcome them home.
You can still see the scars in His hands, the scars of His love.
No more crying. No more hurting. No more sin.
Just God’s big, warm love, forever and ever.
Finally, we are home!
And guess what?
God will make everything new: a new heaven and a new earth, even better than Eden!
Until that day, Jesus asks His friends to tell the whole world the good news, so everyone can find the way back home.

prayer.title: Would you like to follow Jesus?
prayer.intro: It is as easy as A, B, C.

steps.rest: to God that you have sinned, and say you are sorry.
that Jesus is God’s Son, that He died for you, and that He rose again.
to trust Jesus and follow Him every day.

prayer.prayer: “Dear God, I know I have sinned, and I am sorry. Thank You for sending Jesus to die for me and rise again. Please forgive me and make me clean. I want to follow You. In Jesus’ name, amen.”
prayer.note: Talk with a parent, pastor, or grown-up you trust about what you prayed.

grownups.title: For grown-ups
grownups.intro: Try these questions after reading together.
questions: What was the one rule God gave Adam and Eve? Why do you think He gave it?
Why couldn’t the people wash their marks away?
What did Jesus do so we could come back to God?
How do we know Jesus is alive?
Who is someone you could tell the good news to this week?
grownups.note: Every page lists its Bible passages so you can read the full account together.
